title: Gardening updates for November 2026
partialText:
I’ve been doing a lot of digital gardening this week!
 I added content to the guides on Anarchy and Anti-Work (they had previously been placeholders). I wrote guides on the ResizeObserver and MutationObserver APIs. I made some small updates to the Array Methods guide, and removed the standalone guide on Array.prototype.slice().  Enjoy!

title: Yes, I want to pay for that
partialText:

title: Life after coding
partialText:
Lately, I’ve been giving a lot of thought to what I would do if I wasn’t a web developer.
It’s not the first time I’ve thought about this, but the way AI is negatively affecting every aspect of our industry has pushed it top-of-mind again for me.
I’m not alone, either.
I posted about this in a handful of online communities I’m in, and so many developers are struggling with these same feelings.

title: Wasting Time
For and against
partialText:
Yesterday, good internet friend Baldur Bjarnason shared a series of shorts he made on why he doesn’t use generative AI, and it got me thinking about how much of my career has spent being against things.
Early in my career, I was for web performance and accessibility and building cool things.
But as JavaScript frameworks became increasingly ubiquitous, we saw the things I was for start to degrade rapidly. Sites got slower and harder to use.

title: Signal your virtues
partialText:
Virtual signalling is often used as an insult, but it’s good to signal your virtues, actually.
A few months back, I read a story on Bluesky from a hispanic woman who’s immigrant mother got lost in the city. Her phone ran of battery, she didn’t speak much English, and she had no idea how to get home.
She approached a young woman with bright blue hair who was able to use her phone’s translation app to get the mother’s address and help her get home.

title: The SpeechRecognition API
partialText:
There’s an older deaf gentleman in my town who’s very friendly, and likes to communicate with rudimentary hand gestures, but I have a hard time understand what he’s trying to say.
I’d love to learn American Sign Language (ASL) at some point (shoutout King Ron), but until then, I wanted an app that could convert speech into text.
Every transcription app I found required a pretty expensive subscription… so I decided to build my own using web technologies!
